summary: 31-year-old woman at 30 weeks with one day of sudden breathlessness and left pleuritic chest pain; HR 115, SpO₂ 94 %; no leg symptoms. ESC 2019: CTPA or V/Q, LMWH (NOACs not recommended in pregnancy).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Breathless and sharp chest pain in pregnancy
inputs.hpi: 30 weeks pregnant. Since yesterday sudden breathlessness and sharp left-sided chest pain on breathing in. No cough, no fever, no haemoptysis. No calf pain or swelling. BMI 32. Referred to surgical clinic for a pilonidal sinus. Attributed the breathlessness to pregnancy.

exam.general: Breathless on walking into the room.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected pulmonary embolism in pregnancy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected pulmonary embolism at 30 weeks: CTPA or V/Q scan, LMWH while awaiting imaging, obstetric team informed.

mustExclude.note: NOACs are not recommended in pregnancy and VKAs cross the placenta (ESC 2019, class III): a plan offering them without a pregnancy caveat is contraindicated.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Pregnancy-aware PE protocol: LMWH (weight-adjusted) instead of DOACs/warfarin when pregnancyPossible; add CUS first if leg symptoms, then CTPA or V/Q; obstetric involvement.

guideline.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism
guideline.section: Sections 4-6: clinical probability (Wells/Geneva), PERC in low probability, D-dimer only when probability is not high, CTPA; anticoagulation while awaiting results in high/intermediate probability; high-risk (haemodynamically unstable) PE: UFH, bedside echocardiography if CTPA not immediately feasible, systemic thrombolysis; Section 9 pregnancy: D-dimer/CUS/CTPA or V/Q, LMWH (NOACs not recommended in pregnancy)
guideline.citation: Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. Eur Heart J. 2020;41:543-603.

guideline.name: NICE NG158 - Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing
guideline.section: 1.1 DVT: two-level Wells; likely -> proximal leg vein ultrasound within 4 h (interim anticoagulation if delayed); 1.1 PE: two-level Wells; likely (>4) -> CTPA immediately (interim anticoagulation if delayed); unlikely -> D-dimer; PERC when pre-test probability is low
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG158. London: NICE; 2020 (updated 2023).

rationale: Pregnancy permutation. Wells is not validated in pregnancy; ESC 2019 uses D-dimer/CUS/CTPA or V/Q with LMWH treatment. The web PE protocol lists rivaroxaban/apixaban as first-line: this checks whether pregnancy changes the plan.
